misconceptions.description: Assuming decentralized systems are automatically disorganized
misconceptions.trigger: learner describes swarm systems as uncontrolled chaos
misconceptions.feedback: Swarm systems can produce coherent behavior because local rules and feedback signals generate organized emergent patterns.

misconceptions.description: Confusing stigmergy with explicit peer-to-peer messaging
misconceptions.trigger: learner explains stigmergy as direct command exchange
misconceptions.feedback: Stigmergy is indirect coordination through environmental modification or shared traces, not necessarily direct conversation between agents.

misconceptions.description: Assuming adding more agents always improves system quality
misconceptions.trigger: learner recommends larger swarms without considering sensing, interference, or control limits
misconceptions.feedback: Scaling a swarm changes communication load, interference, and task efficiency. More agents can help, but only when the local rules and environment support that scale.

misconceptions.description: Treating swarm inspiration as copying the biological organism rather than the coordination rule
misconceptions.trigger: learner focuses on insect appearance or species identity without describing transferable local control logic
misconceptions.feedback: In swarm engineering, the transferable asset is usually the rule set, signal structure, or allocation mechanism, not the organism's literal shape.

misconceptions.description: Locking onto the first biological analogy and ignoring alternatives
misconceptions.trigger: learner commits to one swarm metaphor before comparing other biological strategies or system constraints
misconceptions.feedback: Good biologically inspired design often compares several analogies, then filters them by function, scale, robustness, and implementation cost to avoid fixation.
